title: Canonical Kummer tower and section-normalized system forgetful data
statement: For a scheme $T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use towers of abelian sheaves and the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a prime $\ell$, let $\mu_\bullet$ be the roots tower of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], let $G^{\rm pow}_\bullet$ have units at every level and power-$\ell$ transitions, and let $G^{\rm const}_\bullet$ have units and identity transitions. Define Kummer data to be the two natural transformations whose components are respectively the root inclusion and the $\ell^{n+1}$-power map, together with their zero composite and short exactness. Define constant integer towers by the constant-system functor; it is additive and exact. For a ring-sheaf tower $B$, use its ringed sequence-site module category from [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Define forgetful data to be the exact additive functor to abelian towers whose section groups, restrictions, transitions and morphism components are the underlying ones of those modules. Its canonical integer-to-unit map is uniquely fixed on every locally constant integer $k$ by $k\mapsto k\cdot1$. These definitions do not assert existence of Kummer data when $\ell$ is not invertible.

proof.text: For constant_exact, unfold the actual constant-system functor. Its map sends a sum to the sum definitionally. Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesLimits_const and preservesColimits_const, then their finite specializations.
proof.elementary: The two preservation instances are Mathlib functor-category results; additivity is reflexivity on each component.

proof.text: For integerGenerator_existsUnique, identify the section groups of the coefficient unit using Forget.sections. Define the map on a lifted integer k as integer cast into B_n(U), followed by equality transport back to the specified group. For a ring homomorphism integer cast commutes with the map (map_intCast). Forget.restrictions and Forget.transitions identify the underlying maps with the actual ringed sequence-site restrictions. Thus the section maps commute with restrictions and adjacent tower transitions.
proof.elementary: Equality elimination reduces heterogeneous group identifications to ordinary equality. The coefficient unit has the ring presheaf itself as its underlying additive presheaf, so map_intCast proves both compatibilities.

proof.text: Use sheafifyLift at every level to extend the constant-presheaf section map to the constant integer sheaf. The identity toSheafify_sheafifyLift proves its prescribed values on constant generators. Apply sheafify_hom_ext to the adjacent transition equations and assemble the level maps by NatTrans.ofOpSequence.
proof.elementary: These are the universal property of sheafification and the constructor of a natural transformation of inverse sequences; the compatibility equations were proved in the previous step.

proof.text: If another tower map has the prescribed generator values, use NatTrans.ext, Sheaf.hom_ext and sheafify_hom_ext. After precomposition with toSheafify, both level maps take every lifted integer to the same cast, so their section maps and hence their tower maps agree.
proof.elementary: Extensionality and the two heterogeneous generator equalities give pointwise equality. Existence and uniqueness together prove the original theorem.
